articles.title: Caleb Williams has one big piece of advice for Cam Ward as a fellow QB: "We have some similarities in our game"
articles.standfirst: The Chicago Bears and Tennessee Titans quarterbacks went head-to-head during joint practices this week.
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears and Tennessee Titans quarterbacks went head-to-head during joint practices this week.
articles.body:
One of the best parts of joint practices during NFL training camp is that it allows players to get up close and personal with each other in a way that's not possible during a regular game.

This week, that meant two of the game's most talented young quarterbacks, Caleb Williams and Cam Ward , went head-to-head. By all accounts, both QBs played well during the practice. While that's expected of Williams coming off of a breakout season, Ward can't say the same.

Caleb Williams advises Cam Ward to "trust" Brian Daboll

Ward's preseason with the Tennessee Titans has left something to be desired. Williams knows all too well what it's like to be a No. 1 overall pick with sky-high expectations , so he decided to leave Ward with one big piece of advice for his second season: to trust his offensive coordinator, Brian Daboll .

I think he has an awesome coordinator that's been in the league for [a while now]. He's been an awesome offensive coordinator and he's been in different places with different quarterbacks. And he has a good track record with different quarterbacks that he's been with. Just believing and trusting in him, and what he's coaching you and teaching you... We have some similarities in our game, being able to make big plays, [it's important to] keep consistent and make the small plays. I'm still working on that myself.

It was no surprise to see Williams take a big step forward in 2025 once he had offensive guru Ben Johnson to learn from. Ward is hoping Daboll and him can develop a similar type of chemistry that Williams and Johnson have.

articles.title: Titans fans enraged by player’s ‘tone-deaf’ outfit after home loss, demand team cut him
articles.standfirst: Julius Chestnut’s pregame costume sparks backlash from angry Titans fans
articles.summary: Julius Chestnut’s pregame costume sparks backlash from angry Titans fans
articles.body:
Julius Chestnut has made himself one of the Tennessee Titans ’ most noticeable players before kickoff this season, though not necessarily for reasons frustrated fans are enjoying.

Chestnut arrived at Nissan Stadium dressed as Green Goblin ahead of Tennessee’s Week 2 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles , continuing a theme that began when he wore a Black Panther costume in Week 1. The second entrance drew a much harsher reaction.

Tennessee had already opened the season with a disappointing loss to the New York Jets , and some supporters saw Chestnut ’s latest outfit as a sign that the backup running back was badly misreading the mood around the franchise.

“Maybe start winning some games before doing this nonsense,” one fan wrote. Another went further: “Cut his ass. I don't need my benchwarmers being this comfortable.”

Chestnut’s costumes now a talking point

The 25-year-old is competing for a role largely behind established running backs Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears , with much of his value expected to come on special teams. That only intensified criticism after video of his Green Goblin arrival circulated online.

“I imagine he's also terrible at reading the vibe in the room,” one supporter wrote. “Tone deaf.” Another described it as “corny behavior from a team that hasn't been good in a while,” while one account said: “I want this dude off my team yesterday. What a clown.”

NFL players regularly use game-day entrances to show personality, and elaborate outfits are nothing new around the league. The issue for Titans fans was less about the costume itself than when it appeared.

Chestnut had dressed as Black Panther before Tennessee’s Week 1 loss, then doubled down with another character while the team was still searching for its first victory.

Robert Saleh already stressed moving on from Week 1

Titans coach Robert Saleh spent the build-up to Philadelphia emphasizing the need to reset quickly after the Jets defeat.

“You're always excited to get back on,” Saleh said earlier in the week. “You know, I think Wednesday is always a great day because it represents the turning of the page.”

He added: “You know, on Monday we went through and had a really good meeting with the group. Tuesday, you're game planning, and today's about turning the page, moving forward, and getting ready for the opponent.”

Some Tennessee supporters clearly wanted that same urgency reflected in everything surrounding the team. One fan wrote: “team is 0-1 & got embarrassed by the Jets. this should get you cut. clearly don't take your job seriously.”

Chestnut ’s outfits have quickly become part of his early-season identity, but the reaction also shows how little patience exists around a struggling team.

If Tennessee starts winning, the costumes may be viewed very differently. Until then, some fans appear much more interested in what Chestnut does after kickoff than what he wears beforehand.

articles.title: Ex-NFL star Chris Johnson shares heartbreaking ALS update on 41st birthday days after Ring of Honor absence
articles.standfirst: Johnson is now relying on an eye-controlled communication device and his family for everyday tasks as he continues his battle with ALS
articles.summary: Johnson is now relying on an eye-controlled communication device and his family for everyday tasks as he continues his battle with ALS
articles.body:
Former NFL star Chris Johnson has opened up about the devastating impact of his ALS diagnosis as the former Tennessee Titans running back marked his 41st birthday.

Speaking to People from his wheelchair, Johnson explained how the disease has dramatically changed his everyday life. He now communicates with the help of a speech-generating tablet controlled by his eyes, while his wife, Brittany , and other family members assist him with many basic tasks.

“ALS has taken away a lot of my independence,” Johnson told People. “As a father, your first instinct is to protect your kids. You don't want them to be scared or feel like their whole world is changing.”

One of the hardest parts of the illness for Johnson is knowing that his mind remains completely active while his body continues to lose its abilities.

Johnson was diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in May 2025 after initially noticing weakness in his right hand. Since then, the disease has progressed significantly.

He can no longer speak independently and requires a CPAP machine to assist with breathing. His family also helps him eat, get dressed and complete physical exercises.

Brittany has become Johnson’s primary caregiver, a responsibility she has described as her calling. Johnson has stressed that ALS hasn't affected only him, but has changed the lives of everyone in his household.

Chris Johnson remains focused on his family

Despite the enormous challenges, Johnson continues to look toward the future and remains deeply involved in his children's lives. His sons still play football, and although his own experience has changed the way he views the sport, he hasn't told them to give it up.

“I want them to understand the risks and take care of their bodies,” said Johnson . “If football's what they love, and that's the path they choose, I'm going to support them. More than anything, I want my kids to be healthy, happy and able to build lives they love.”

His diagnosis has also prompted questions about whether his years playing football could have contributed to his illness. Johnson has said his doctors haven't told him that football or head trauma caused his ALS, and they haven't identified one specific reason for his diagnosis.

Research has nevertheless examined possible links between football and ALS. A 2026 study of former NFL players found an elevated rate of ALS deaths, particularly among players who died before reaching 50.

Researchers said the findings warrant further investigation into whether repetitive head impacts could be connected to motor-neuron disease. The research doesn't prove that football caused Johnson's illness.

His health struggles also forced the Titans to postpone his Ring of Honor induction ceremony in Nashville. Johnson and his family were unable to make the trip because of his rapidly progressing condition.

Still, Johnson remains hopeful. He has indicated that treatment is helping slow the progression of the disease, although his long-term prognosis remains uncertain.

His biggest motivation is his family. Johnson wants to watch his sons grow into adulthood and hopes he'll someday be able to walk his daughter down the aisle.

articles.title: Titans QB Cam Ward’s controversial remarks in response to criticism of his play: "People are weird"
articles.standfirst: Ward faces growing scrutiny as Tennessee stumbles to an 0-3 start
articles.summary: Ward faces growing scrutiny as Tennessee stumbles to an 0-3 start
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward has found himself at the center of growing criticism after the team's winless opening to the 2026 season, but he's refusing to let the noise consume him.

The Titans fell to 0-3 following Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants, with Ward's late interception becoming the defining moment of the defeat.

With Tennessee threatening near the goal line and only 24 seconds remaining, Ward was picked off by Jevon Holland , ending the team's final opportunity to take the lead.

Ward acknowledged that he hasn't delivered his best football in crucial moments, but he's also had to deal with criticism that has extended beyond the field. Threats have reportedly been directed toward Ward and members of his family on social media.

Asked about the situation Wednesday, Ward offered a blunt response: "People are weird."

He then added: “They can say whatever they want at the end of the day, but I think football will take care of a lot of it. My family knows the position I'm in and what I've wanted my whole life.

“They're in this position as well with me … Every adverse situation I have, I'm going to take on. It's really just about making plays on the football field. If I do that, we do that as a team, it's going to cut all that out."

The situation became serious enough for Ward's sister to address it publicly. She argued that fans have every right to criticize performances and express frustration with a team's results, but said targeting players' relatives crosses a line.

Ward's numbers through three games help explain some of the scrutiny. He's completed 55 of 88 passes for 504 yards, two touchdowns and one interception, while the Titans have struggled to consistently generate offense.

Robert Saleh explains what may be affecting Ward

Head coach Robert Saleh has suggested that some of Ward's struggles could be connected to the punishment he endured during his rookie season. Ward was sacked 55 times in 2025, tied for the league lead, and Saleh said the quarterback may have "some PTSD" from that experience.

“You’ve got to remember the young man was sacked however many times last year so I’m sure there’s some PTSD there,” Saleh said.

Saleh believes Ward is making progress, particularly in his ability to trust the offensive line and maintain his footwork. However, the coach also acknowledged that Ward can revert to old habits later in games.

That inconsistency was evident against New York. Tennessee managed only 54 yards in the first half after opening the game with five consecutive three-and-out possessions. The offense improved after halftime, but Ward couldn't complete the comeback.

Ward also accepted responsibility for his performance, saying he didn't play his best when the team needed him most. The second-year quarterback knows those critical situations are where improvement will be measured.

The Titans now turn their attention to the Baltimore Ravens, with Houston waiting the following week. Tennessee's next stretch will give Ward another opportunity to respond to the criticism through his play.

articles.title: Should the Titans trade for Shedeur Sanders? Cam Ward isn't working out
articles.standfirst: Cam Ward and the Titans have stumbled to an 0-5 start, fueling questions about Tennessee's future at quarterback. Could Shedeur Sanders emerge as the franchise's next answer?
articles.summary: Cam Ward and the Titans have stumbled to an 0-5 start, fueling questions about Tennessee's future at quarterback. Could Shedeur Sanders emerge as the franchise's next answer?
articles.body:
It has long been no secret that the Tennessee Titans continue their struggle to find a better version of themselves, and the reality is that Cam Ward is not bringing them closer to the standards that raised hopes when they had the opportunity to select him with the first overall pick in the 2025 Draft.

Now, many fans are beginning to question whether it was the best choice at the time, especially since a name like Shedeur Sanders was available—a quarterback who watched his Draft stock collapse until he was selected by the Cleveland Browns in the fifth round.

If Cam Ward, who had a successful stint with the Miami Hurricanes , was not the solution, several fans are asking whether it is possible to trade him at this moment for Shedeur, who is currently watching from the sidelines as Deshaun Watson has regained the starting job in Cleveland.

“Just Trade Cam Ward for Shedeur Sanders,” proposes the user @MichaelJesusS7 on X , something that does not seem far-fetched.

Can the Titans make a trade for Shedeur Sanders?

Yes, the Tennessee Titans can propose a trade to the Cleveland Browns for the former Colorado Buffaloes quarterback, as long as they do so before November 10 , the NFL’s trade deadline .

If this were to happen, it would undoubtedly be a devastating blow to Cam Ward’s career , the player on whom they bet the entire future of the franchise.

A disastrous week vs. the Houston Texans

The 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans on October 11 deepened the Tennessee Titans’ crisis. They suffered their fifth consecutive defeat and recorded their worst start to a season since 2009 , sitting at a dismal 0-5 (0-1 in the AFC South).

Cam Ward’s team hit rock bottom in a campaign marked by disappointment. Tennessee managed just 187 total yards—their lowest offensive output of the year—and once again showed their inability to compete.

Although the Titans arrived with some hope after losing by six points or fewer in their three previous games, they were never able to challenge the Texans, who, in a Week 5 divisional matchup, secured their first win of the season and improved to 1-4 (1-1 in the AFC South) .

Ward finished the game 23-of-36 for 170 yards, with no touchdowns and one interception . He was also sacked three times, while Tennessee’s offense reached the red zone only once.

articles.title: Cam Ward lashes out at critics following the Titans' fifth straight loss
articles.standfirst: Tennessee suffered a blowout loss to the Houston Texans in Week 5
articles.summary: Tennessee suffered a blowout loss to the Houston Texans in Week 5
articles.body:
C am Ward is refusing to accept a losing mentality despite the Tennessee Titans falling to 0-5 after a 26-3 defeat to the Houston Texans as the rookie quarterback faced a blunt question from reporters about whether he had become accustomed to losing. Houston earned its first victory of the season behind C.J. Stroud on October 11, who threw for 261 yards and a touchdown while adding a rushing score as the Texans forced two turnovers, and Will Anderson Jr. recorded three of their four sacks.

Tennessee managed just three points, failing to score a touchdown while finishing with only 187 total yards as Ward completed 23 passes for 170 yards and was sacked four times as the Texans controlled the contest on both sides of the ball, but the 24-year-old dismissed the question of being familiar with losing emphatically. “No, I’m not a loser,” Ward said. “The record may say that we are that right now, but at the end of the day you have to go through some stuff to get wins. We attack this each and every day, but for that, no. “If you’re able to look at everybody in our locker room’s track record, we all won games at a high level. We’re looking forward to doing that in the long run.” Ward has completed 63.2% of his passes through five games, accumulating 896 passing yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions. His season-low 12.8 QBR highlighted the difficulties he is experiencing as the Titans search for answers on offense.

Titans have little choice but to keep backing their quarterback

Ward 's development has been complicated by instability around him as Tennessee dismissed Brian Callahan during the quarterback’s rookie season before hiring Saleh in the offseason, with Brian Daboll arriving as offensive coordinator. But the changes have yet to produce the turnaround the franchise hoped for, and Sunday's defeat also extended Tennessee 's losing streak to six games dating back to last season, while the Titans have now lost 11 consecutive AFC South contests. Houston took control early on via a field goal from Tennessee , recovering a Tyjae Spears fumble before Jake Hansen intercepted Ward , and the Texans dominated thereafter, outgaining the Titans 225-49 and scoring 16 unanswered points to put the game beyond reach. There is still time for Ward to improve, and five games alone do not determine whether a young quarterback can succeed, and he will be grateful to have the backing of his head coach. “Cam’s our starting quarterback,” Saleh said. “We’re going to give him every opportunity to be successful this year, and we’re going to continue working with him, grinding with him and trying to help him get better.”

articles.title: Jordan Elliott sparks an NFL scandal: the Titans fired the player after he went to his car to get a gun.
articles.standfirst: The franchise initially limited itself to reporting that Elliott had been removed from the team after reviewing an “incident” that occurred at its facilities.
articles.summary: The franchise initially limited itself to reporting that Elliott had been removed from the team after reviewing an “incident” that occurred at its facilities.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans made a drastic decision regarding Jordan Elliott. The 28-year-old defensive tackle was cut after an incident that occurred during a practice which, according to multiple reports, began with an argument between teammates and ended with Elliott heading to his car to retrieve a firearm.

'“Following our review of the incident, we have made the decision to release Elliott from our roster,” the Titans said.'

The NFL is already investigating what happened

Details about what happened began to emerge afterward. According to reports, Elliott allegedly went to his vehicle to retrieve a weapon after the altercation during practice.

Nashville police did not receive any reports related to the episode, and no injuries were reported.

Elliott's departure from Tennessee does not necessarily mean the end of the case. The NFL is reviewing the incident and could determine whether any additional type of sanction is warranted for the player.

Titans coach Robert Saleh called what happened a “terrible lapse in judgment,” although he also said he hoped Elliott could get the help he needed.

Saleh especially highlighted Franklin-Myers' intervention, who managed to keep the situation from escalating.

Elliott leaves Tennessee after just five games

Elliott did not participate in practice the day after the incident for what the team initially described as “personal reasons.” He also did not play on Sunday in Tennessee’s 26-20 victory over the Indianapolis Colts.

Five days after the episode, the Titans decided to definitively end their relationship with the player.

Elliott had arrived in Tennessee during the offseason on a two-year, eight-million-dollar contract. In his first five games with the team, he recorded 11 tackles.

Selected by the Cleveland Browns in the third round of the 2020 Draft, the defender also spent time with the San Francisco 49ers before reuniting with Saleh in Tennessee.

Now, his time with the Titans ended abruptly and his future in the NFL remains subject to the league’s review. The team has already made its decision; any additional consequences are still to be determined.

Saleh especially highlighted Franklin-Myers' intervention, who managed to keep the situation from escalating.
Elliott leaves Tennessee after just five games

Elliott did not participate in practice the day after the incident for what the team initially described as “personal reasons.” He also did not play on Sunday in Tennessee’s 26-20 victory over the Indianapolis Colts.
Five days after the episode, the Titans decided to definitively end their relationship with the player.
Elliott had arrived in Tennessee during the offseason on a two-year, eight-million-dollar contract. In his first five games with the team, he recorded 11 tackles.
Selected by the Cleveland Browns in the third round of the 2020 Draft, the defender also spent time with the San Francisco 49ers before reuniting with Saleh in Tennessee.

Now, his time with the Titans ended abruptly and his future in the NFL remains subject to the league’s review. The team has already made its decision; any additional consequences are still to be determined.
